goodnews.b: Emory staff created a free online course to help faith communities navigate artificial intelligence and the spiritual questions it raises.

local.h: Poll: 3 Mass. ballot questions in virtual tie
local.b: A Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll of 500 registered voters found three of the nine ballot questions, including all-party primaries, in a virtual tie two weeks before Election Day.
local.title: 3 Mass. ballot question races are locked in virtual ties, new poll suggests

local.h: Shawn Oliver quits lieutenant governor race
local.b: The New Bedford city councilor suspended his GOP campaign for lieutenant governor after an OUI charge, hours after running mate Mike Minogue called on him to step aside.

local.h: SEIU backs Giannoulias in Chicago mayor's race
local.b: SEIU Locals 1 and 73, which gave over $4.5 million to Mayor Johnson's 2023 campaign, endorsed Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias.
local.title: Feud between progressive unions that put Mayor Johnson in office yields Giannoulias key endorsement

local.h: Chicago mayoral hopefuls file petition stacks
local.b: Candidates wheeled in thousands of nominating petitions at the start of a weeklong filing period for the February election. They need 12,500 valid signatures.

local.h: Endangered Species Act changes threaten Illinois species
local.b: Trump administration changes to how the law is interpreted could put 24 endangered and 12 threatened species in Illinois at greater risk.

local.h: Early voting opens in all 50 Chicago wards
local.b: Expanded in-person early voting for the Nov. 3 general election began Monday at sites in every ward across the city.

local.h: City Colleges reach deal hours before strike
local.b: City Colleges of Chicago and its faculty union reached a four-year tentative contract at 3:45 a.m., hours before a strike was set to begin Monday.

local.h: $125M settlement approved for Garden Grove tank
local.b: GKN Aerospace will fund up to $100 million in claims for residents and businesses forced out when about 50,000 people evacuated over the failing chemical tank.
local.title: $125M settlement approved for Garden Grove chemical tank incident

local.h: LA County emergency official sues over Eaton Fire
local.b: Nicholas Vaquero of the Office of Emergency Management alleges retaliation after he complained the county failed to properly staff its response to the deadly Eaton Fire.
local.title: Emergency manager sues LA County, alleging retaliation over Eaton Fire whistleblower complaints

local.h: Long Beach neighbors confront ICE after arrest
local.b: Residents say they blocked federal agents from detaining Ricardo Gonzalez, a U.S. citizen, after an agent tackled him off an e-bike and broke his arm.

local.h: NYC proposes rules for AI customer service bots
local.b: A proposed rule would require businesses to disclose AI chatbots and let customers talk to a person instead. The city says it is the first of its kind.
local.title: NYC proposes crackdown down on AI customer service chatbots

local.h: MTA train yards in disrepair, watchdog says
local.b: Plants grow through holes in the roof of the Bronx East 180th Street yard, where 2 and 5 trains are serviced, and water drips onto electrical equipment.
local.title: MTA train yards are in such bad shape plants are growing out of the roof, watchdog says

local.h: Hate crime charge in Queens bagel shop attack
local.b: Police charged a 22-year-old Fresh Meadows man with targeting Bagels & Co., a kosher shop on Union Turnpike, hurling dirt at its storefront and Israeli flags.
local.title: Queens man charged with hate crime at Jewish-owned bagel shop displaying Israeli flags

local.h: NYC team to help residents keep SNAP, Medicaid
local.b: Mayor Mamdani launched a Health and Affordability Resource Team of outreach workers to help New Yorkers keep benefits as federal eligibility rules change.
local.title: Mamdani launches new team to help NYers keep SNAP, Medicaid benefits

local.h: Ex-buildings chief Eric Ulrich goes on trial
local.b: Eric Ulrich, Eric Adams' former buildings commissioner, heads to trial three years after his arrest on charges of taking more than $150,000 in bribes.
local.title: Eric Adams' NYC buildings boss Eric Ulrich heads to trial, 3 years after arrest

local.h: NYC sues law firm over bogus trip-and-fall claims
local.b: The city's law department is going after Lower Manhattan firm Asher & Associates over lawsuits it says were fraudulent, including a $1 million sidewalk claim.
local.title: NYC sues personal injury law firm accused of bogus trip-and-fall claims

goodnews.h: Coney Island's 1890s lighthouse may be landmarked
goodnews.b: The Landmarks Preservation Commission voted to hold a hearing on the 70-foot lighthouse, which has guided boats for more than 135 years, and its keeper's house.
goodnews.title: Coney Island's small, 1890s lighthouse may be landmarked by the city

goodnews.h: Free 2-K expands to the Bronx and Staten Island
goodnews.b: Every school district in the Bronx and Staten Island will offer free preschool seats for 2-year-olds next fall, as the city adds 10,000 seats.
goodnews.title: These are the NYC neighborhoods that will get free 2-K next fall

goodnews.h: New NYC site helps find mental health care
goodnews.b: NYC Mental Health Connect lists more than 600 behavioral health providers across the five boroughs, searchable by service, symptoms, age, location and insurance.
goodnews.title: Need help with mental health or addiction services? NYC has a new tool.

local.h: Curfew in parts of Paris, protests banned
local.b: Police imposed an 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew around Place de la République and Les Halles and banned demonstrations in several neighbourhoods overnight.
local.title: New Paris curfew ordered on Tuesday for parts of city

local.h: Storm and flood warnings for southern France
local.b: Météo-France put Hérault, Gard, Var, Lozère and Bouches-du-Rhône on orange alert for violent Mediterranean storms, with up to 200mm of rain possible.

local.h: Protesters block the Louvre amid unrest
local.b: Protesters blocked the Louvre entrance on Monday after weekend cost-of-living demonstrations turned violent. Macron ordered a security review.

local.h: Arrest, anti-terror probe over Limoges town hall fire
local.b: Police arrested a man believed linked to the ultra-left and called in anti-terror investigators over the fire that collapsed the 1883 town hall's roof and belfry during weekend rioting.
local.title: France arrests suspect and calls in anti-terror police over Limoges town hall fire

local.h: 250,000 in Washington could lose Medicaid
local.b: New Medicaid work requirements for low-income adults start in January, and up to 250,000 Washington residents could lose coverage.
local.title: Why 250,000 WA residents might lose their Medicaid next year
